content: 1. The systemic exposure of talazoparib, a substrate of the breast cancer resistance protein (BCRP), may increase when coadministered with certain agents. If coadministration cannot be avoided, monitor for potential adverse reactions. 2. Cobicistat reduces the effects of tamoxifen by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4, which is involved in tamoxifen metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. CYP3A4 inhibition decreases the conversion of tamoxifen to its active metabolite, N-desmethyl tamoxifen, which has similar biological activity. 3. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of tamsulosin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 4. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of tazemetostat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors should not be coadministered with tazemetostat. 5. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of teniposide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 6. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of ticagrelor by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 7. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of cobicistat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 8. Cobicistat increases the levels of tofacitinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministered with potent CYP3A4 inhibitors, reduce the tofacitinib dose to 5 mg once daily. 9. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of tolterodine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 10. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of tolvaptan by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 11. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of topotecan by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. For oral topotecan, avoid concomitant use of P-gp inhibitors. The interaction with IV topotecan may be less severe but still clinically significant. 12. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of toremifene by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 13. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of trabectedin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If a strong CYP3A inhibitor must be used, administer it one week after trabectedin infusion and discontinue it the day before the next infusion. 14. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of trazodone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 15. Tucatinib increases the levels or effects of cobicistat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Avoid using tucatinib with CYP3A substrates where minimal concentration changes may lead to serious or life-threatening toxicities. If unavoidable, reduce the CYP3A substrate dose according to product labeling. 16. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of valbenazine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 17. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of vemurafenib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 18. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of vilanterol/fluticasone furoate (inhaled) by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 19. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of vilazodone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 20. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of vincristine liposomal by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 21. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of vorapaxar by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 22. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of zolpidem by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 23. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of abemaciclib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors increase plasma levels of abemaciclib and its metabolites, requiring dose reduction. If the strong CYP3A inhibitor is discontinued, increase the abemaciclib dose after 3-5 half-lives of the inhibitor to the pre-inhibitor dose. 24. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of alfentanil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 25. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of amiodarone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Clinical monitoring is recommended when coadministered with antiarrhythmics. 26. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of amitriptyline by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Carefully titrate the antidepressant dose to the desired effect, using the lowest feasible initial or maintenance dose, and monitor for antidepressant response. 27. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of amlodipine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 28. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of amoxapine by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Carefully titrate the antidepressant dose to the desired effect, using the lowest feasible initial or maintenance dose, and monitor for antidepressant response. 29. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of apalutamide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Coadministration with strong CYP3A4 or CYP2C8 inhibitors does not require initial dosage modification, but dose reduction may be needed based on tolerability. 30. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of apixaban by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 31. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of aripiprazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Reduce the aripiprazole dose by 25%, and by approximately 50% if coadministered with both a CYP3A4 inhibitor and a CYP2D6 inhibitor. 32. Cobicistat decreases the levels or effects of artemether/lumefantrine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Monitor for potential decreases in antimalarial efficacy or QT prolongation. 33. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of atogepant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. The recommended atogepant dosage is 10 mg orally once daily when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 34. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of atorvastatin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. For HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors not contraindicated with cobicistat, the dose should not exceed 20 mg/day. 35. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of avatrombopag by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. When treating ITP, coadministration with moderate or strong dual CYP2C9/3A4 inhibitors requires a decreased avatrombopag starting dose. Refer to the drug monograph for specific recommendations. 36. Belzutifan decreases the levels or effects of cobicistat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. If coadministration with sensitive CYP3A4 substrates is unavoidable, consider increasing the sensitive CYP3A4 substrate dose according to its prescribing information. 37. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of benzhydrocodone/acetaminophen by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase hydrocodone plasma concentrations, potentially resulting in fatal respiratory depression. 38. Cobicistat increases the levels of berotralstat, a BCRP substrate. Use caution and monitor. Monitor for adverse effects when coadministered with a BCRP inhibitor. 39. Cobicistat increases the levels of betrixaban by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. Decrease the betrixaban dose to 80 mg orally once, then 40 mg orally daily if coadministered with a P-gp inhibitor. 40. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of bortezomib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 41. Bosentan decreases the levels or effects of cobicistat by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Bosentan dose reduction is required. Refer to the prescribing information for recommended dosage adjustments. 42. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of brentuximab vedotin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 43. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of brexpiprazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Administer half the usual brexpiprazole dose when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 44. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of bromocriptine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 45. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of budesonide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 46. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of buprenorphine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely.
